findings.F1: The American IPA ˈrɛk.ɚd is the noun's stress; the verb is rɪˈkɔrd, as the entry's own notes say.
findings.F2: 'record a photo' is not a natural collocation; one takes a photo.
findings.F3: Sense 1 participle phrases (officially recorded and so on) are typed adverb + verb instead of phrase.
findings.F4: Sense 2 participle phrases (secretly recorded, digitally recorded) are typed adverb + verb instead of phrase.
findings.F5: Sense 3 conflates an instrument showing a measurement with a person or company achieving a result; 'record a temperature' is duplicated with sense 1.
findings.F6: The verb/noun stress contrast is stated in pronunciation.notes, usage_note, adaptation.pronunciation and word_family, breaking one fact, one field.
findings.F7: The usage note wrongly limits the noun 'record' (a thing made) to vinyl discs; it is common for an album in any format.
findings.F8: The compare note on tape falsely calls tape the older word and puts a history claim outside etymology.
findings.F9: take-v is listed as a synonym of record though it is only a light-verb partner.
findings.F10: adaptation.grammar restates the sense grammar values without naming a specific trap.
